children: Veteran market strategist Tom Lee says the next six months could be the most important stretch for inflation, a period that may determine whether the stock market finally gets relief from elevated bond yields.

Speaking on CNBC, the Fundstrat co-founder said investors are still trying to understand why yields have moved higher and whether those levels will persist. He also argued that rising yields can actually strengthen the position of large, well-funded companies because financing becomes harder for weaker competitors.
That, Lee said, could help explain why the Magnificent Seven remain relatively resilient even as yields rise.

I still think the next six months will be the most important because if inflation starts to decline, this is not because of the Fed hikes that happened last week. It's because of the policy that's already in place, Lee said. He added that lower inflation could eventually allow the Federal Reserve to walk back some of that hawkishness.
Lee sees several reasons inflation could ease.

He said a September 30 change in PCE methodology could reduce the reported year-over-year rate by roughly 20 to 40 basis points. He also expects tariff effects and flash-memory price effects to fade over time.

Lee argued that if oil remains near $100, it would stop adding meaningfully to inflation six months from now because the year-over-year comparison would normalize. For inflation to accelerate materially, he said housing would need to rise more sharply, oil would likely need to move toward $150, and memory prices would need another significant jump.
For stock market investors, Lee's call comes down to whether inflation starts moving lower before higher yields inflict more damage.
If inflation cools, the Fed could turn less hawkish and bond-market pressure could ease.
Lee said the probability is high that inflation will be lower six months from now.
And if that's the case, the market can really breathe a sigh of relief, he said.
The risk is straightforward: if inflation stays elevated while yields remain high, valuations could face more pressure.
That makes the next six months a critical test for both inflation and the stock market.

title: Veteran Analyst Sends Big Signal to Stock Market Investors
